verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 6.6, j row of the key table: '`@` and three whole numbers of degrees, the turn of the picture'. SPEC.md 6.6 Validation: 'a known key with a value that does not parse' loads the default with the notice. decisions/P4-A2.md '2026-10-17 P4-A2: the j value' records normalisation only. Both passages support the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: Read at b9b8504 in the worktree, detached there with a clean status and nothing installed. Only the oracle script was run. (1) The codec: urlCodec.ts:238 PROJECTION /^(coxeter|xyz:(\d+),(\d+),(\d+))(@(-?\d+),(-?\d+),(-?\d+))?$/ has no length bound, and lines 385-393 store raw.j as text. The angles never pass intToken (urlCodec.ts:141-145). For every other integer the codec uses intToken, which refuses a non-safe integer under rule 1 ('is not a safe integer'). P4-A3's entry 'polish, wave 4.4' relies on that rule for rings: 'A ring beyond the safe integers never reaches the tool: the codec refuses it as a value that does not parse'. (2) The tool: projector.ts:261 reads Number(m[6..8]), :271 computes ((t % 360) + 360) % 360, and studio.ts:82 (admit) stores formatProjection(parsed). (3) P4-A2 'the j value' records the same regex and 'formatProjection writes ... angles reduced to 0..359'. It also says 'Angles are kept as parsed ... reduced only when written or turned. What the specification left open: normalisation.' It records no bound and no rounding, and NaN is outside the 0..359 it promises. (4) 6.6 has no [D] mark. It bounds g (512 characters) and s (40 digits per entry) but not j. So an angle either parses as a whole number, and the turn is that number, or it does not parse, and the notice shows. Exact arithmetic in my scratch script: (2^53+1) mod 360 = 33, while float(2^53+1) mod 360 = 32.0, the build's value; (10^23-1) mod 360 = 279 and (10^400-1) mod 360 = 279. (5) Phase: T10 is phase 4 (SPEC 4, 'T10. Geometry Studio (phase 4)') and the gate is G4. (6) Records: reports/gate-G4.md names b9b8504 and has no item on j. No round 1 finding covers it, and there is no merge-P4-redteam report on disk. Part of `expected` is weaker than stated: 7.4 'Copy link always encodes the current state' holds literally, since Copy link encodes the NaN state the tool holds. The defect is that this state is not the one the link names.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed because 6.6 has no clause that permits rounding an angle or turning it into NaN, and it names no bound on j. R2 failed because the finding reads the j row and Validation correctly; only its 7.4 point is weaker than stated. R3 failed because T10 is phase 4 at gate G4. R4 failed because no oracle function parses links, and exact arithmetic gives 33 and 279, not 32 and NaN. R5 failed because 6.6 is not [D], and P4-A2 records only normalisation to 0..359. R6 failed because there is no record. Severity: a stated behaviour of 6.6 is wrong (the tool should show the turn the link names, or else the notice). That is the rubric's major item, not wording.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 6.6 Data export: 'the derived tables shown on screen (positions, roots, edges, matrices), all integers as JSON numbers when safe and as decimal strings otherwise'. decisions/RT-FIX-P3-export-long.md: 'a rational whose denominator is 1 is an integer in the data export' and 'tools hand values, not display text, to the export'. Both support the finding.
verdicts.evidence: Read at b9b8504 (clean detached worktree). (1) T11: t11/model.ts:307 (averagedOf) copies c.form_value, the engine's string (CONTRACTS 2.4: averagedRootsType ... form_value: string). exportData (~:690-705) puts avg.classes into derived.averaged unchanged, while bigPositions and foldedPositions go through integerOut. (2) T10: T10GeometryStudio.svelte:956 writes edgeLengthsSquared as lengthText(l.squared), which is String() of a float rounded to 6 decimals (uniform.ts:99-102). By SPEC 2.14 [V] these values are 2 d_i a_i^2, an integer on every named type. The oracle gives L.symmetrizer = [1,1,1] on A3 and [1,3] on G2, so the exact values are 2, and 2 and 6, as the finding says. (3) RT-FIX-P3-export-long says 'an integral rational counts among the integers of 6.6' and that SPEC 5.7 rule 4 (golden form_value stored as text) 'governs golden_data.json, not the export'. Its second entry required T3, T4 and T6 to hand values, not display text, to the export. (4) The other records allow nothing different. P4-A4 'the table view and the exports' lists derived.averaged and applies the integer rule only to the positions, with no record that form_value is exported as text. The P1-A2 'data export' record says floats stay numbers. P4-A3 has no export entry. (5) 6.6 is not [D], and T10 and T11 are phase 4 at gate G4. (6) Round 1: P3-RT-04-05 was fixed for T3 and T4 and P3-RT-04-02 for export.ts and T6. This is the same cause in two new tools, not an open tracked item. gate-G4.md lists nothing on it.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed because 6.6's integer rule has no 'may' and no qualifying clause. R2 failed because the finding applies the rule to integers shown on screen (form values 1 and 2, squared lengths 2 and 6). R3 failed because both tools are phase 4 at G4. R4 failed because the golden form_value text is governed by 5.7 rule 4, which RT-FIX-P3-export-long confines to the golden file, and the oracle's exact lengths are integers. R5 failed because the recorded decision is on the finding's side and nothing records these fields as text. R6 failed because there is no open record. Severity: an exported field breaks a stated rule, which is the rubric's major item; this matches both round 1 verdicts on P3-RT-04-05, which raised it to major.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 7.4 History API: 'After a move the address bar is updated with replaceState, half a second after the last move of a burst'. SPEC.md 6.6: 'only instances the reader has changed are written'. build-plan/agents/P1-A2-site-infra.md 5.6 (line 173): 'Nothing is written on load or hydration; the address bar changes only after the reader acts.' decisions/P1-A2.md 'History API'. None of these permits a write on load.
verdicts.evidence: Read at b9b8504 (clean detached worktree). (1) ToolFrame.svelte:99-110 calls registerInstance(id, defaults ?? toolState, ..., toolState) once at hydration, and every later change of toolState goes to stateChanged. (2) history.ts:68-78: stateChanged schedules one replaceState whenever encodeState(state) differs from the recorded state. (3) T10GeometryStudio.svelte:535-550 decodes window.location.search in nextTask after hydration and calls applyLink. The link's state therefore reaches stateChanged as a change, and a write follows about 500 ms later. (4) Records: P1-A2 says '`initial` the state shown now; registering writes nothing'. That record covers registration only, not a link applied after registration. The plan forbids any write on load or hydration (line 173 and checklist line 278). P4-A3 'repair, wave 4.3' records only the scheduling ('A link is read one task after hydration') and nothing about the address bar. P4-A2 records the j normalisation (370 written as 10), which this write makes visible but does not cause. (5) 7.4 has no [D] mark (the heading of 7.6 does). No section 10 default concerns history. (6) History is phase 1 and the tools named are phases 1 to 4, all within G4. gate-G4.md has no item on it. A grep of round1-confirmed-A.json, round1-confirmed-B.json, round1-deferred.json and RESULTS.md for replaceState and 'on load' finds no such finding.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed because 7.4 ties replaceState to moves and 6.6 to instances the reader changed, and nothing permits normalising the bar on load. R2 failed because the finding quotes 7.4, 6.6 and the P1-A2 plan line correctly, and the P1-A2 record ('registering writes nothing') does not cover a link applied after registration. R3 failed because every part is within phases 1 to 4. R4 does not apply, since no oracle function covers history. R5 failed because no [D] passage or recorded decision allows the write. R6 failed because there is no record. Severity none: SPEC 7.4 says when the bar is written but does not in words forbid a write on load; that prohibition is the plan's (P1-A2 5.6), so the rubric does not clearly name this major or minor.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 2.14 Edge lengths [V]: 'the edge from λ to R_iλ has squared length a_i^2(α_i,α_i)=2d_ia_i^2', and 'The site draws integer orbits exactly and offers "make uniform" as a display option computed in floating point [D]'. reference/verify.py lines 1118-1127 check this exactly, and golden wythoff_note states it. decisions/P4-A3.md 'make uniform' says the lengths 'agree with 2 d_i a_i^2 within 1e-9'. All of these support the finding.
verdicts.evidence: Oracle run: python3 -I script, with sys.path set to the gate commit's reference/ in the clean detached worktree. (1) Exact values: L.symmetrizer(cartan('A',3)) = [1,1,1], so 2 d_i a_i^2 = 3411272 at every node of (1306,1306,1306) and 1999996000002 for (999999,999999,999999). G2 has symmetrizer [1,3], giving 1999996000002 and 5999988000006. (2) The same base edges measured on the oracle's own float picture (euclidean_basis, weight_to_root_coords, fire): A3 at 1306 gives 3411272.000000255, 3411271.9999994934 and 3411272.000000257. Rounded to 6 decimals these are '3411272' and '3411271.999999', exactly the build's observed pair. A3 at 999999 gives 1999996000002.1494, 1999996000001.7026 and 1999996000002.1501. G2 gives 1999996000001.9976 and 5999988000006.0. The float measurement is therefore off by about 5e-7 at 1306 and up to 0.3 at 999999. The oracle's exact statement (verify.py: weight_inner(e,e) == lam_i^2 Bg[i][i]) is the finding's expected. (3) The build: uniform.ts:84-107 measures |y0-y1|^2 in floats, and lengthText rounds to 6 decimals. T10GeometryStudio.svelte:275-276 and 1018-1020 show the results as 'squared lengths of the edges at the start', with data-count set to the number of distinct texts, also when make uniform is off. (4) Records: P4-A3 caps rings at RING_MAX = 999999, so 1306 is in range. Its 'make uniform' entry promises agreement within 1e-9, which the oracle's float run shows fails from 1306 on. The 2.14 [D] covers make uniform, but the finding's main case is an integer orbit with make uniform 'not needed', which 2.14 says is drawn exactly. (5) Part of the finding misreads its source: SPEC 5.1 E-1 is about engine arithmetic and does not say 'a value shown as a number must be that number'. (6) 4.0 Long numbers [D]: '1999996000001.7036' has 13 integer digits and is shown unshortened, which breaks the [D] text. (7) T10 is phase 4 at G4. Neither gate-G4.md nor round 1 has a record.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed because the [D] of 2.14 covers make uniform only, and the integer orbit is to be exact. R2 holds only in part: E-1 is misquoted, but the cause stands on the [V] sentence of 2.14. R3 failed because T10 is phase 4 at G4. R4 failed because the oracle's exact statement gives one value, 3411272; its float picture reproduces the build's error, which shows the defect rather than permitting it. R5 failed because P4-A3's own record promises agreement within 1e-9, which does not hold. R6 failed because there is no record. Severity none: a wrong value for a [V] quantity in a tool output is the rubric's major item (a stated behaviour or field wrong). The owner may consider whether the blocker item 'a mathematical statement presented as fact that is wrong' applies, since data-count 2 asserts two edge lengths where there is one.
